title: Bore contour: a linear lead with a Ramp entry under carried stock gives RapidInStock on the second level

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

A bore-side contour (`Side::Inside`) has carried stock over Top Z (#1559, `Approach::material_top`). It uses `Lead::Linear { length: 2.0 }` and `Entry3D::Ramp`, with `Links::PLANAR` or with the level link `Link::Retract`. Verify with the stock top at the carried stock gives `RapidInStock` on the descent into the second level.

Reproduction (motion crate, the fixture of `crates/motion/tests/one_descent.rs`):
- hole: a circle of radius 10, tool diameter 6, Top Z 0, Bottom Z -6, stepdown 2;
- `links.approach.material_top = Some(5.0)`;
- verify with `stock_top_z: 5.0`, `Mode::Area`.

Result: `verify [RapidInStock { at: 2673 }]`. Move 2673 is the rapid from Z 25 to Z 2.0 at (0.232, -6.546). Move 2674 is the substituted axial dive from Z 2 to Z -2 (note "the ramp's chord is blocked - axial dive on the floor instead").

`main` at `fac6c8e8d` gives the same result. PR #2013 does not change it.

## What is not known

A probe found each footprint point of that rapid within 2.87 mm of a planar feed at Z 0 that comes before it (tool radius 3). Thus the rapid can be a false conviction of the verify column law. It can also be a real rapid into a cusp of carried stock. In the application the verify warning blocks the post, so the output is not silent. This issue must find which of the two it is.

## Done means

- The cause is known: the verify reading or the dive start.
- The fix removes the warning or makes the dive start over the stock.
- The case `carried bore lead linear Ramp planar/retract` in `the_bore_contour_under_carried_stock_never_rapids_into_it` (`crates/motion/tests/one_descent.rs`, PR #2013) is no longer skipped.
